teachBack.purpose: The canonical APS repository is Sigil's semantic authority for ASH Pattern System behavior: the full F2^9 state space (512 states), the fixed 16-member [9,4,4] doubly-even codeword set with 32 orbits, XOR-by-codeword transitions, realm and orbit identity, the seven system-state classes, recovery/fallback/containment/SAFE_HALT semantics, the fifteen-field diagnostic schema with nine-field semantic identity, and the rule-ID taxonomy. Sigil's visible-glyph engine, status gateways, guardrails, and diagnostics must preserve these invariants wherever they model ASH behavior.
teachBack.nonPurpose: The canonical repository defines no programming language, operating system, runtime, build system, package, platform implementation, or emitted artifact tree, and it is not a runtime dependency of Sigil. It does not authorize importing ASH-Pattern-System source into the product, and it does not define numerology input policy, profile-to-state mapping, or personal identity semantics (those are product-owned decisions recorded under product policy). Field note: product.baselineCommit identifies the Sigil repository baseline for this record and is intentionally distinct from system.sourceCommit, which is the authority-container revision; the profile binding requirement applies to system fields versus profile fields, not to product.baselineCommit.
teachBack.productLocalImplementation: Sources/RFSigilAPSIntegration (SigilAPSIntegrationGateway status plus source-coverage evidence records plus SigilAPSIntegrationModule) is the product-owned APS integration module. tools/sigil_guardrails enforces the canonical 16-member codeword literal set and the diagnostic rule-ID taxonomy in product code. docs/ash-trace records the source-to-output trace, findings, verification cases, and conformance documentation. Any future ASH state machine in Sigil will be product-owned code conformant to the pinned rc.3 specification, with conformance evidence structured by the downstream handoff requirements.
teachBack.permittedExternalDependencies: none. The profile allowedRuntimeProducts and allowedDevelopmentTools are both empty; the canonical repository authorizes no package or native target dependency. Sigil consumes no APS code today.
teachBack.externalOnlyMaterials: All of flynn33/ASH-Pattern-System remains upstream: specs (core, algorithms, registries, interfaces, verification), canonical-data, conformance corpus, schemas, examples, handoff-templates, tools, governance, and completion evidence. Sigil cites the repository by pinned commit in product documentation and evidence records; repository URLs appear as citations only and never in dependency declarations.
teachBack.templateAndExampleUse: handoff-templates define the shape of downstream conformance evidence (module mapping document, verification report, diagnostics conformance report, materialization-boundary report, deviation log, acceptance judgment); Sigil uses them to structure docs/ash-trace and future conformance documentation. examples/ and the conformance/ corpus are verification material that establishes expected results; neither enters runtime targets.
teachBack.conformanceProof: docs/ash-trace/trace-ledger.json maps each product behavior to a supported, evidenced-substitution, or unresolved source basis with retrieval evidence; the strict guardrails validator enforces the 16-member codeword literal set and the rule-ID taxonomy in product code; scripts/verify-sigil-guardrails.sh plus swift test provide the local verification route; the realization validator verifies this contract and the absence of prohibited acquisition against the product checkout.
